"PROJECT: GAME STUDIO TYCOON

Professional Mobile Game Development

ROLE

Act as a senior mobile game developer, game designer, software architect, 3D environment designer, and simulation systems engineer.

Your task is to help me create a complete, polished mobile Game Studio Tycoon simulation game from scratch.

GAME VISION

The player starts as an independent game developer working from a tiny bedroom.

Their objective is to build a successful gaming company, hire employees, develop games, expand offices, research technology, compete with rival companies, and eventually become the world's biggest gaming corporation.

TARGET PLATFORM

- Android
- iOS
- Single-player
- Landscape orientation
- Touchscreen optimized
- Offline playable with local saving

RECOMMENDED ENGINE

Use Unity with C# and URP for mobile optimization.

Use modular, maintainable, object-oriented programming.

CORE GAMEPLAY SYSTEMS

1. BUSINESS MANAGEMENT

- Company creation.
- Starting capital.
- Revenue and expenses.
- Company reputation.
- Bankruptcy and recovery.
- Financial reports.

2. GAME DEVELOPMENT

- Game genre selection.
- Platform selection.
- Game size selection.
- Graphics quality.
- Feature selection.
- Development progress.
- Development budget.
- Quality calculation.
- Game publishing.
- Sales simulation.
- Reviews and ratings.

3. EMPLOYEE MANAGEMENT

- Employee recruitment.
- Different job roles.
- Skill and experience.
- Salary and productivity.
- Employee happiness.
- Training and promotions.
- Employee management dashboard.

4. OFFICE MANAGEMENT

- Office purchasing and expansion.
- Desks and workstations.
- Computer upgrades.
- Meeting rooms.
- Server rooms.
- Research laboratories.
- Office decorations.
- Employee capacity.

5. MARKET SIMULATION

- AI competing companies.
- Market trends.
- Genre popularity.
- Customer demand.
- Market share.
- Game rankings.
- Competitor releases.

6. RESEARCH SYSTEM

- Technology tree.
- New game engines.
- Graphics technologies.
- Artificial intelligence.
- Multiplayer technology.
- Console development.
- VR and AR.

7. MARKETING SYSTEM

- Social media campaigns.
- Influencer promotions.
- Advertisements.
- Game trailers.
- Pre-orders.
- Launch events.

8. PROGRESSION

- Bedroom Developer.
- Indie Studio.
- Professional Studio.
- AAA Developer.
- Global Gaming Corporation.

9. SPECIAL EVENTS

- Gaming conventions.
- Awards.
- Unexpected expenses.
- Employee resignations.
- Viral game releases.
- Market crashes.
- Competitor acquisitions.

10. SAVE SYSTEM

- Save company progress.
- Save employees.
- Save money and reputation.
- Save unlocked technologies.
- Save office configuration.
- Automatic saving.
- Manual saving.
- Versioned save data.

GRAPHICS AND PRESENTATION

- Stylized 3D environments.
- Isometric camera.
- Detailed office interiors.
- Animated employees.
- Interactive workstations.
- Dynamic lighting.
- Day and night cycle.
- Smooth camera movement.
- Optimized mobile rendering.

USER INTERFACE

Create professional mobile-friendly screens:

- Main dashboard.
- Office view.
- Game development screen.
- Employee management.
- Finance dashboard.
- Research tree.
- Marketing dashboard.
- Market leaderboard.
- Settings.
- Save/load interface.

MOBILE OPTIMIZATION

- Stable performance on mid-range Android devices.
- Object pooling.
- Optimized 3D models.
- Efficient UI updates.
- Reduced unnecessary calculations.
- Memory management.
- Battery-conscious simulation.
- Touch-friendly controls.

SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE

Use separate systems and classes:

- GameManager
- CompanyManager
- EconomyManager
- EmployeeManager
- OfficeManager
- GameDevelopmentManager
- MarketManager
- ResearchManager
- MarketingManager
- SaveManager
- UIManager
- EventManager

Keep systems independent and communicate through clean interfaces and events.

DEVELOPMENT RULES

1. Build the project from zero.
2. Divide development into phases.
3. Explain every Unity setup step.
4. Give exact folder paths.
5. Provide complete (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, polished, playable mobile Game Studio Tycoon game from scratch or adapt the existing project.

## Requirements
- Android/iOS, landscape, single-player, offline play with local saves; touchscreen-friendly phone/tablet UI.
- Include business finances, game development and publishing, employees, office expansion, market/rivals, research, marketing, progression, events, and save/load.
- Stylized 3D/isometric presentation, mobile optimization, and modular systems. Unity with C# and URP was recommended; explain setup steps and exact paths.

## Decisions
- The repository contained no existing game, so work began on a browser-based playable prototype.
- Implemented a responsive web game with hand-drawn SVG studio illustration and localStorage persistence; native Unity project/build remains unimplemented.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added modular simulation systems for company, economy, employees, office, development, market, research, marketing, events, and versioned saves.
- Added responsive UI screens for Overview, Studio, Games, Team, Finance, Research, Marketing, and Market.
- Added game production/publishing, daily simulation, hiring/training, expansion, campaigns, research unlocks, rivals, events, and manual/automatic local saves.

### Active
- Validate the browser game, fix any issues, and improve/complete the implementation.

### Blocked
- No known blockers.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and run the prototype; test core gameplay and mobile layouts.
2. Add or adjust startup instructions and document how to play.
3. Clarify that the current deliverable is a web prototype, or proceed toward the originally recommended Unity implementation if required.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App entry and metadata.
- `styles.css`: Responsive visual design and mobile layout.
- `src/app.js`: UI rendering and interaction handlers.
- `src/simulation.js`: Simulation systems, gameplay state, and save/load.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- No validation or screenshot/browser checks have been performed.
- `start.sh` expects the harness-provided `RUNTIME_DIR`; no standalone web server configuration was added.

# Studio Story — Game Studio Tycoon

Studio Story is a playable, responsive **web prototype** of a single-player game-studio management sim. It runs locally in a modern browser and stores your studio save in that browser's local storage. It is not a native Android/iOS or Unity build.

## Run locally

Requirements: Python 3 and a modern browser. No package install or internet connection is required to run the game itself (the optional Google Fonts connection only affects typography).

```bash
./serve.sh
```

Open [http://localhost:8000](http://localhost:8000). To use another port, set `PORT`:

```bash
PORT=8080 ./serve.sh
```

You can also serve the project with any static HTTP server. The game uses ES modules, so opening `index.html` directly as a `file://` URL is not supported by all browsers.

## How to play

- Start on **Overview** and check your cash, reputation, community, and current project.
- Open **Games** to choose a title, genre, platform, project size, graphics quality, and optional features. Start production, then advance days until the game ships.
- Advance time with **Work a day**. Each day updates production, payroll and rent, sales, marketing, employee happiness, market trends, and occasional events.
- Grow the company in **Team** (hire/train), **Studio** (expand/decorate), **Research**, and **Marketing**. Browse competitors and trends in **Market** and cash flow in **Finance**.
- Progress is automatically saved in this browser. Use the save button for a manual save. Clearing this browser's site data will remove the local save.

## Current scope

The prototype includes the main tycoon loop, responsive desktop/mobile layouts, and local saves. It does **not** currently include native mobile packaging, a service worker/PWA install flow, cloud sync, or cross-device saves. Static game assets are local; Google Fonts are an optional external request and system fonts are used if unavailable.

## Objective
- Build and validate a polished, playable Game Studio Tycoon prototype, adapting the existing project.
- Current deliverable is a responsive browser game; native Android/iOS implementation is outside its current scope.

## Requirements
- Original goal includes offline single-player play, local saves, touch-friendly UI, studio finances, development and publishing, employees, office growth, market/rivals, research, marketing, events, and progression.
- Serve the ES-module game over HTTP; the prototype has localStorage saves but no service worker/PWA installation flow.

## Decisions
- Adapted the existing project into a modular browser-based tycoon game with responsive screens and SVG studio artwork.
- Added a standalone Python HTTP server launcher and gameplay/scope documentation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented Overview, Studio, Games, Team, Finance, Research, Marketing, and Market screens and core simulation systems.
- Added `serve.sh` and updated `README.md` with run instructions, gameplay guidance, and scope limitations.
- `node --check src/app.js` and `node --check src/simulation.js` pass.
- Browser-tested project kickoff, advancing seven days, game release, sales, and save persistence after reload. “Mosslight Valley” shipped; state persisted at Day 8 with one published game.
- At a 390×844 browser viewport, mobile navigation rendered and no horizontal document overflow was reported.

### Active
- Finish responsive checks across phone/tablet sizes and key pages; address any defects found.
- Consider adding a favicon to resolve the sole observed console error (`/favicon.ico` 404).

### Blocked
- Native Unity/mobile build is not implemented.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser checks on mobile/tablet viewports, especially gameplay controls, forms, and navigation on screens beyond Overview/Games.
2. Fix the missing favicon if appropriate, then rerun browser console and syntax checks.
3. Review the final diff and preserve the existing uncommitted project changes.

## Relevant Files
- `README.md`: local startup instructions, gameplay, and scope limitations.
- `serve.sh`: local static-server launcher; defaults to port 8000, configurable with `PORT`.
- `index.html`: browser entry point.
- `styles.css`: desktop/mobile layouts.
- `src/app.js`: rendered screens and interaction handlers.
- `src/simulation.js`: gameplay systems, state, and save/load.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked and `README.md` is modified.
- A server was started at `http://localhost:3002`; the project launcher serves at `http://localhost:8000` by default.
- Playwright’s only observed console error is the missing `/favicon.ico` 404.

## Objective
- Complete and validate a polished, playable Game Studio Tycoon browser prototype adapted from the existing project.
- Preserve current project changes; native Android/iOS implementation is out of scope.

## Requirements
- Offline single-player gameplay, local saves, touch-friendly responsive UI, finances, development and publishing, employees, office growth, market/rivals, research, marketing, events, and progression.
- Serve the ES-module game over HTTP.

## Decisions
- Adapted the existing project into a modular browser game with responsive screens and SVG studio artwork.
- Added a Python HTTP server launcher and documented gameplay and scope.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented Overview, Studio, Games, Team, Finance, Research, Marketing, and Market screens and core simulation systems.
- Added `serve.sh`, updated `README.md`, and added `favicon.svg` and page description metadata.
- Expanded mobile navigation to all eight screens, added safe-area padding and a two-row layout below 360px.
- `node --check src/app.js` and `node --check src/simulation.js` pass; `git diff --check` passes.
- Browser-tested all eight screens at widths 320–820px with no horizontal overflow; navigation worked at each screen. Favicon endpoint returns HTTP 200 and links to `/favicon.svg`.
- Previously browser-tested project kickoff, seven-day progression, release, sales, and save persistence after reload. “Mosslight Valley” shipped; save persisted at Day 8 with one published game.

### Active
- Fix and recheck a small-screen horizontal overflow on the Overview screen at desktop/tablet widths just above the 820px mobile breakpoint; observed 4px overflow at widths 821–900px.
- Recheck browser console and final diff/status after the responsive fix.

### Blocked
- Native Unity/mobile build is not implemented.

## Next Move
1. Inspect Overview layout styles, especially `.right-stack` and its children; resolve the 4px overflow between 821–900px without affecting phone/tablet layout.
2. Reload browser after CSS edits, re-test all screens at phone, breakpoint, and desktop sizes, and check console/favicon requests.
3. Review `git status` and final diff while preserving existing uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `README.md`: startup instructions, gameplay, and scope.
- `serve.sh`: local static-server launcher.
- `index.html`: browser entry point, description metadata, and favicon link.
- `favicon.svg`: game icon.
- `styles.css`: responsive layouts, navigation, and safe-area rules.
- `src/app.js`: rendered screens and interaction handlers.
- `src/simulation.js`: gameplay systems, state, and save/load.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. `README.md` is modified; game, launcher, metadata, icon, and several other files are untracked. Preserve them.
- Browser server is available at `http://localhost:3002`; browser session is open.
- At 320–820px, all eight screens passed navigation checks with no horizontal overflow. At 821–900px, Overview had 4px overflow; other tested pages did not.
- `favicon.svg` responds HTTP 200; prior missing `/favicon.ico` error has been addressed by linking the SVG favicon.

+
